message_preview: Scammers posing as admins of the FiveM roleplay server "Revolution RP" contacted me on Discord, had me share my screen, then install AnyDesk and took control of my PC. They ran a file called "verif.exe", crashed the PC and claimed they had encrypted it and stolen my data. They demanded a ransom in Solana (SOL), which I paid in three transfers (about 500, 400 and 100 EUR, roughly 1,000 EUR in total) during the night of 27-28 October 2026. They also took over my Discord account and deleted the conversation.

message_preview:
On 18 September 2026 (KST), a Korean medicine hospital in Busan, South Korea was hit by the NightSpire ransomware group (file extension ".nspire", ransom note "[NSPIRE_MSG].txt").




Timeline:

- ~16 Aug 2026: Attackers gained access to our internal network and installed AnyDesk on our Oracle database (EMR) server for persistent remote access. They remained inside for about one month, most likely exfiltrating patient data.

- 18 Sep 2026, 07:29-07:32 KST (17 Sep 22:29 UTC): Our EMR database server (Oracle datafiles, ~90 GB) and our NAS backup server were both encrypted. All backups were destroyed.

- The ransom note demanded 10% of yearly revenue and threatened to publish stolen patient data on their Tor leak site and to report us to regulators.We negotiated through their Tor chat portal. Initial demand was USD 50,000; final agreed amount was USD 20,000, paid in Bitcoin (0.25 BTC total) to the attacker's wallet in two transactions on 19 Sep 2026.




We are reporting the attacker's Bitcoin address and both transaction IDs so exchanges and investigators can flag and trace these funds. This attack involved theft of medical patient data. We have also reported the incident to Korean authorities (KISA, police, PIPC).

On August 2, 2026, I received an unsolicited extortion email from the address abdrabo@almajdwarnerlewis.com.sa (display name: Charlotte Lee).




The email contained psychological manipulation text aimed at creating panic, along with a compromised password from an old data breach to make the threat appear genuine. Attached to the email was an image file (90a838...12c.png) containing a standardized sextortion ransom note (Internal ID: d3ovl1).




In the attachment, the scammer falsely claimed to have installed a Trojan virus on my device, recorded non-existent video footage, and harvested my contact lists. They demanded a payment of $4300 USD sent to their Bitcoin wallet address: bc1qzvtdfv7v8jkcxr39cwps8wrfgkvxaxqxp4s8nk to prevent the alleged release of the footage.




No financial loss occurred, as the attachment was not opened/downloaded and no funds were transferred.

message_preview: On the evening of 07/28, an attacker that had infiltrated the account of my friend on discord had privately messaged me. They inquired if I would join a server of Minecraft to help with a birthday gift for someone. The attacker did a good job of mimicking the communication style of my friend. The attacker sent me files of Minecraft modpacks for Curseforge, however, I was suspicious and scanned the files using the website Virustotal. The only issue was picked up by KasperSky but there was a community note saying it was a false positive. I didn't give the files permission. The attacker then resulted in giving me a dropbox link to another personalized modpack. That link was how the attacker had managed to get into my Google Chrome Session and Discord. From there, the attacker was able to retrieve my PII and take control of my discord and threatened to ruin me if I did not pay. I had to comply because I had no knowledge of how to remove the attacker's hook into my discord and Google accounts. The attacker had me pay them in Bitcoin through Cashapp. The address they had me send the bitcoin was bc1qk303r4uq7jk8klqz7ty2lshvdklvp9wpu936vn. After the ransom, I had investigated the address through BitRef website and through a series of transactions, I found that the address the attacker had given me was an alt or burner that they would put into the main account of bc1qns9f7yfx3ry9lj6yz7c9er0vwa0ye2eklpzqfw.
